verses.1: In the year four hundred and seventy, during the reign of Jeroboam, king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah.
verses.2: He reigned for thirteen years. He also ruled for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jeckelyah from Jerusalem.
verses.3: And he did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, just as his father Amasya had done.
verses.4: Only the idols remained unchanged. The people continued to worship and offer sacrifices to those idols.
verses.5: And Jehovah struck the king, and he became sick until the day he died. Then he was taken to the prison house. And Yotham, son of the king, ruled over the land.
verses.6: And all the words of Azariah, and everything he did, are written in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.7: And Azariah lay down with his ancestors. They buried him with his ancestors in the city of David. Yotham was his son, who ruled after him.
verses.8: In the thirty-seventh year of Azariah, king of Judah, Zekheriah, son of Yeravam, ruled over Israel in Samaria for six years.
verses.9: And they did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as their ancestors had done. They continued in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel astray.
verses.10: And Shalum, the son of Yabesh, was bound to him. The people accepted him as their king, and they killed him. Then he became their king.
verses.11: And the additional words of Zekarya are written on the book of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.12: It is the word of Jehovah, who said to Yehu, “The children of Rebi’im shall sit upon the throne of Israel.” And so it was.
verses.13: Shlomo, son of Jeabesh, ruled for thirty-five years during the reign of Uzziah, king of Judah. He ruled for many years in Shechem.
verses.14: And Menachem, son of Gadi, came from Tirzah. He went to Shomron and killed Shalum, son of Yabesh, in Shomron. Then he became king over them.
verses.15: And the additional words of Shalom, and those words that are recorded on the book of days for the kings of Israel.
verses.16: Then He will take away all its treasures and everything that is inside it. He will also destroy its borders, because it never opened any of its doors at all.
verses.17: In the thirty-sixth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi ruled over Israel for twelve years in Samaria.
verses.18: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD. He was never satisfied with his sins. Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who led Israel astray throughout his entire life.
verses.19: The king of Assyria came upon the land. He gave Pul ten thousand pieces of silver, so that he could hold the kingdom in his hands.
verses.20: And he distributed the money among all the rulers of Israel, so that each ruler would give fifty shekels as a gift to the king of Assyria. Then the king of Assyria sat on his throne, but he did not remain there in that land.
verses.21: And all the words of Menachem, and everything he did, are recorded in the book of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.22: And Menachem lay down with his fathers. And Pekhiah, his son, became his king under him.
verses.23: In the year fifty, during the reign of Azariah, king of Judah, Pekachiah son of Menachem ruled over Israel in Shomron. That was in the second year of his reign.
verses.24: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not stop his wickedness, just as Rehoboam son of Nebat had done, who led Israel astray.
verses.25: And Rehoboam’s son, Abijah, took hold of him. He killed him in the palace of the king, along with his lion. There were also fifty men from the tribe of Judah who joined him in killing him. Then Abijah became king after him.
verses.26: And all the words of the wise men, and everything they did, are recorded in the book of the days of Israel’s kings.
verses.27: In the year five hundred and twenty, Azariah, king of Judah, ruled over Israel in Samaria for forty years.
verses.28: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD. He was not different from the sins of Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who led Israel astray.
verses.29: In the time of King Pekah of Israel, King Sennacherib of Assyria came and took away Jerusalem. He took away the Temple of God, Zion, and all the other holy places. He also took away the Valley of Hinnom, the Garden of Gilead, and the entire land of Naphtali. Assyria destroyed everything.
verses.30: And Rehoboam, son of Elah, married Phakhah, son of Ramla. He married her and killed her. Then he became king over Israel at the age of forty years, in the year of Jotham’s reign.
verses.31: And all the words of Pehach, and everything he did, are recorded in the book of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.32: In the second year of his reign, King Yosafat son of Remaliah became king over Israel. Uziya son of Yoyada became king over Judah.
verses.33: He reigned for forty-five years. He ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. His mother’s name was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok.
verses.34: And he did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, just as his father Uziah had done.
verses.35: Only the altars did not stop being worshipped and sacrificed upon them. It was from these altars that he built the upper gate of the Temple of Jehovah.
verses.36: And the additional words of Jotham, which he did, are not written in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.37: In those days, Jehovah began to send rulers from Aram to rule over Judah. Among them was Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah son of Remaliah.
verses.38: And Yotham lay down with his fathers. He was buried with his fathers in the city of David, his father’s city. And Ahaz his son reigned after him.
